trust_decision.summary: The proxy decides which identity (X-Remote-User/Group/Extra-*) the backend shard trusts over the proxy's mTLS connection. Inbound copies are stripped only when the proxy itself authenticated the user. A request the proxy passes through unauthenticated (no client cert, no additional auth) keeps client-supplied identity headers, and the shard trusts them.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'does not strip inbound X-Remote-* headers', and SetAuthHeaders is the only stripping helper; its package doc names exactly those headers. It already strips, so the engineer must then work out which caller skips it.

fix_sites.entry_point: internal helper; new ClearAuthHeaders split out of SetAuthHeaders (fix.diff:19-40), used by both proxies

kcp-front-proxy HTTPS: every path mapping in the mapping file (/clusters/, /services/..., default '/') wired at pkg/proxy/mapping.go:104, reached unauthenticated via pkg/proxy/filters/filters.go:61-68

kcp server (shard/standalone) --additional-mappings-file path mappings wired at pkg/server/localproxy.go:300; WithLocalProxy runs before authentication (pkg/server/config.go:568,599), so no user is ever in context
fix_sites.module_kind: second implementation in kcp server package (pkg/server)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: pkg/server/localproxy.go:324-332 (near-copy of pkg/proxy/proxy.go:59-67 in another package; comment at pkg/server/localproxy.go:242-245 says it mirrors proxy/mapping.go)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The pinned tree's own test comment states the unauthenticated pass-through is a deliberate contract and that such requests 'never reach a shard mapping' (pkg/proxy/proxy_test.go:215-221). For the local proxy, a solver can argue it is 'mainly for standalone mode without a real front-proxy' (pkg/server/localproxy.go:101-103) and that it forwards over an insecure transport with no client cert (pkg/server/localproxy.go:276-277,314-320), so no backend would trust the headers.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Unauthenticated pass-through must keep working: bearer-token clients with no client cert are forwarded so the shard can authenticate them itself. Rejecting no-user requests at the proxy, or stripping more than the identity headers, breaks that. Authenticated requests must still be stamped with the real identity, including URL-escaped extra keys.

O6_input_shapes: X-Remote-Extra-* keys of any case, matched by case-insensitive prefix (warrant, scopes)
custom header names and prefix per mapping entry (pkg/proxy/mapping.go:94-102, pkg/server/proxy/types/mapping.go:30-32)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: UID identity header (--requestheader-uid-headers, e.g. X-Remote-Uid) is never stripped or stamped by either proxy, so a client-supplied UID reaches a shard configured to trust it, on both the authenticated and unauthenticated branches
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: UID headers are feature-gated (RemoteRequestHeaderUID) and the kcp topologies only configure user/group/extra headers (cmd/sharded-test-server/shard.go:90-92), so a solver can call UID unsupported. The flag is still exposed to shards at pkg/server/options/flags.go:82.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point; the trust config is in pkg/server/options

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the mounted-workspace reverse proxy forwards client headers to the mount URL with no identity handling; a variant that sends to a trusted backend over the shard's client cert would be a third copy
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it already hand-builds a reverse proxy with a TODO to wire a real cert (pkg/server/localproxy.go:178); adding a client cert there without stamping is a plausible maintainer change

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a wildcard or no-cluster mapping path that skips the resolver could be given its own short-circuit proxy handler that bypasses WithProxyAuthHeaders
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the mapping handler already special-cases empty and '*' cluster names and delegates directly

O8b_injection_room.sibling: case-sensitive or canonicalised prefix match on extra headers (a how-type parser differential against the shard's prefix matching)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the matching logic is hand-written; upstream requestheader matching is case-insensitive

O9_family: authentication bypass via trusted identity headers forwarded by a proxy (spoofable request-header identity)

O10_build.project_tests: unit tests: pkg/proxy/proxy_test.go, pkg/proxy/authheaders/authheaders_test.go, pkg/server/localproxy_test.go (httptest, offline). e2e test/e2e/proxy/header_injection_test.go needs a multi-shard kcp plus etcd and is not suitable for offline use.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add an else-branch strip only in pkg/proxy/proxy.go (or reject no-user requests in WithOptionalAuthentication), missing the pkg/server/localproxy.go copy and breaking bearer-token pass-through.

out_of_scope_notes: httputil.ReverseProxy drops hop-by-hop headers named in a client 'Connection' header after the identity is stamped; whether that can remove stamped X-Remote-* headers so the shard falls back to the proxy cert identity was not checked.
pkg/virtual/initializingworkspaces/builder/build.go:281-298 strips Impersonate-* headers. That is a different protection (impersonation), not request-header identity.
pkg/server/handler.go:68-108 forwards to the virtual workspace server via an impersonating transport, not request-header identity.
unverified: O8 UID route: assumes the upstream k8s requestheader authenticator honours --requestheader-uid-headers when the RemoteRequestHeaderUID gate is on; vendored k8s code was not read.
Whether local-proxy mapping backends trust request headers: the transport there presents no client cert (pkg/server/localproxy.go:314-320), so the local-proxy site may be low impact in practice.

The advisory summary says 'any authenticated client'; the code shows the gap is the front-proxy pass-through for clients the proxy did not authenticate (e.g. bearer tokens the shard authenticates). This reading is taken from the code and diff only; the advisory text was not available.
